drugs.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP)
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic vasopressin analog that concentrates the urine and cuts nighttime urine production; it controls bedwetting but does not cure it
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyponatremia, especially in elderly patients on other medications, sometimes enough to need admission
drugs.use: Primary nocturnal enuresis when dry nights matter, such as sleepovers (the bed-wetting alarm is the cure); nighttime incontinence in adults, with caution

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate
drugs.mechanism: Extra buffer draws H+ out of cells in exchange for K+ moving in; it alkalinizes the urine more than the serum, so some toxins leave faster and some stones form less readily
drugs.adverseEffects: Not for DKA (worse outcomes in studies), rhabdomyolysis (fewer myoglobin casts but no AKI or mortality benefit) or simply an unwanted pH number
drugs.use: Hyperkalemia; tricyclic and other Na+ channel blocker overdose; urine alkalinization in salicylate overdose; oral alkali in CKD acidosis to keep serum HCO3- above 23

drugs.name: Acetazolamide
drugs.mechanism: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor: bicarbonate is lost in the urine, producing a metabolic acidosis that drives ventilation up
drugs.use: Prophylaxis before a high-altitude ascent; very severe metabolic alkalosis; considered when respiratory alkalosis dominates early salicylate poisoning

drugs.name: Fomepizole
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, so ethylene glycol and methanol are converted to their toxic acids slowly enough for the liver to cope
drugs.use: Antidote for antifreeze or methanol poisoning; without it, IV (or even oral) ethanol competes for the enzyme; add thiamine and pyridoxine, and dialysis in severe cases
